samples.description_en: In the Invoices scene, moving the pointer without holding a button drives the pink control sphere through ordinary invoice spheres. They overlap without push-back, bounce, or rotational feedback, while ordinary invoice spheres still collide normally with one another.

During motion in the Invoices scene, ordinary invoice spheres show inverted perspective: spheres closer to the camera become smaller while distant spheres become larger. Their motion paths and collision ranges remain normal.

In the Projects panel, hovering NOT HUMBLE shows the 50 beaches preview, while hovering 50 beaches shows the NOT HUMBLE preview. The NOT HUMBLE preview in the home-page Featured Project remains correct.

When switching to the second through fifth feature demonstrations, the laptop screen continues showing the previous video until the display has already rotated back toward the user, then abruptly changes to the current feature video.
The amount and percentage at the top of Real Time Value continue updating on schedule, but the line chart below remains frozen at its initial data instead of advancing with the same live window.
Clicking the Histogram legend in the MACD chart makes the bars disappear or reappear instantly instead of passing through the normal soft blurred transition.
The pale-green RSI reference line is still labeled “30 (Oversold),” but it moves to the minimum value of the current RSI series when the asset or time range changes instead of remaining fixed at 30.
After returning from any planet detail to the overview, Mercury and Venus remain frozen at their pre-detail positions while the other planets continue orbiting normally.

After Cancel is clicked in the Security Gateway, the confirmation card disappears immediately but the darkened backdrop remains for about one second. During that interval, visible desktop icons and the taskbar still cannot be clicked.
When the Hero capability word changes from “AI-powered” to “data-driven,” the outgoing word's final “ed” remains visible at the upper right for about 0.5 seconds alongside the fully entered new word.
While pressing and dragging in the Draw a line scene, the colored 2D trail is still drawn normally, but nearby particles no longer develop the localized mosaic distortion around the trail.
The entrance cat remains visible, but both pupils stay in their default forward-facing position regardless of horizontal or vertical pointer movement and no longer follow the pointer smoothly.

After the pink control sphere is dragged and the mouse is released, invoice spheres continue to be attracted at full strength toward the last mouse position for about one second, and new unpressed pointer movement is ignored during that interval. The attraction then stops abruptly.

In Neon Drift, the vehicle and obstacles still move according to forward travel, but the ground texture also moves toward the front of the vehicle, creating conflicting motion references between the road and obstacles.

If the Music Player window is minimized while playing and then restored, its play icon and progress display continue to indicate playback, but the actual audio has stopped and the waveform on the right is no longer moving.
If the user changes targets or exits before a planet-detail transition finishes, returning to the overview stops every orbit. The speed slider remains visible and draggable but cannot restore motion.
After the lower-left background music is paused, both the audio and its control indicate a paused state, but the speaker in the upper-right of the room continues pulsing at the previous rhythm.
While the hero is scrolled, the sky, mountains, and planets remain visible, but every background layer stays at its initial position instead of moving vertically at different parallax rates.

The Hero capability words still rotate in the same order and timing, but each transition becomes a whole-word vertical scroll. The outgoing word no longer exits toward the upper right with blur, and the incoming word no longer resolves character by character from a blurred state.
While moving through the corridor past side doors such as About, Gallery, Studio, or Contact, the camera remains straight ahead instead of gradually leaning toward the side of the nearby door.

Entering the same room door from different positions and viewing directions always returns the user to one fixed corridor position and orientation instead of restoring the actual view used for that entrance.
In the Hero, Ideas, Concepts, Designs, and Code and their icons are replaced instantly at each transition point instead of sliding vertically into and out of the fixed-height window.

On entering Professional Work Experience, the central colored timeline is already fully visible and no longer reveals or retreats progressively with downward or upward scrolling. The experience cards and text still enter normally.
In the skills section, the 3D technology logos in all five cards remain at fixed heights and orientations instead of continuing their subtle idle floating and rotation.

As the Interactive Web color fill changes width, low progress shows only the leftmost colors and later colors appear progressively as the fill grows. The complete red-to-purple gradient is no longer present at every visible width.
The 3D logo in the Hero remains at its initial orientation and no longer changes horizontal yaw or vertical pitch as the pointer moves across the page.
The Hero's 3D logo still changes orientation with pointer movement, but both horizontal yaw and vertical pitch always move opposite to the pointer direction.
After the home-page 3D background is dragged and released, it remains permanently at the last angle instead of returning to its continuous slow automatic rotation.
When the pointer enters a Skills card or the Education timeline, the background point-and-line network stops responding to it and resumes only after the pointer leaves those content areas.
A stepped-on hex tile turns orange and is removed on schedule, but stays fully opaque throughout its remaining lifetime and then disappears instantly instead of fading continuously.
Before the character lands from its first jump, pressing Space or clicking Jump grants another upward impulse, creating a double jump instead of allowing the natural descent to continue.
The lower-left joystick remains visible and shows a pressed state, but dragging it in any direction no longer moves or turns the character. Keyboard movement remains functional.
The colored decorative balls in the Hero remain visible but stay fixed when the pointer moves, so their parallax response is absent. The rings and other hero elements are unaffected.
In Features, the first three cards still reveal their low-opacity background images on hover, but the last three show only their text, icon, and Explore more; their background images never appear.

After the Growing Together numbers complete their first count, leaving the statistics area and returning makes all four numbers alone reset to zero and count again while the cards remain in their completed entrance state.

During a sustained vertical drag on the interactive globe, rotation stops before reaching a pole, and further dragging cannot cross the pole or turn the globe upside down. Horizontal dragging remains normal.

When the countdown seconds roll from 00 to 59, the minute value remains unchanged for one extra tick and decreases only on the next second, briefly making the displayed remaining time increase instead of decreasing monotonically.

On the first entrance into the “Subscribe. But why?” section, the container, text, input group, and angled decoration only fade in at their final positions, with none of the original upward or opposite-direction sliding motion.

During the horizontal brand-image loop, a long blank interval appears after both content groups leave, followed by an abrupt jump back to the first group's starting point instead of a seamless continuous cycle.

After Next is clicked in Testimonials, the active card's name and text have changed to the next customer while the avatar remains from the previous customer for about 300 ms, briefly combining two records.
Clicking any main navigation item still scrolls to the correct section, but the desktop underline and mobile blue-text highlight remain on the previously clicked item instead of the current target.

When the pointer moves on any page, the background particles, nearby connecting lines, and glowing color fields continue moving, but the cyan matrix grid remains fixed to the viewport and no longer produces subtle pointer-driven parallax.
In Graphics / Shadow Cascades, turning off Every Frame makes all visible cloud shadows pause and then jump together instead of continuing to move smoothly.

Once a clear begins, the entire board ignores clicks and drags until every burst, fall, refill, and cascade has finished, including pieces that are already settled and not involved in the current animation.
Before all newly refilled pieces have reached their bookshelf cells, the next automatic match, burst, score update, and combo round begins, causing settling and the next resolution round to overlap.

A column-clearing special created by a horizontal four-piece match has the correct appearance and position, but activating it by tapping or dragging clears only itself and leaves the rest of its column intact.

Pieces cleared by a regular three-piece match still leave afterimages that fly to the cauldron, but ordinary pieces cleared by any special ability only burst in their cells and disappear without flying to the cauldron.
Easy uses six regular piece types while Hard uses only four, reversing the piece pools associated with those difficulties. Normal still uses five, and special-piece formation is unchanged.

When switching between quality presets in a way that also changes antialiasing, the dropdown, saved value, and refresh notice all show the new preset, but grass density and campfire particles remain at the previous preset until the page is refreshed.
A lightning strike still shows its blue bolt, plays the nearby thunder sound, and shakes the camera, but the strike point no longer emits the orange-yellow ground sparks that should burst outward.

After the camera view is adjusted and lightning is triggered manually, the shake begins from the current view but ends by jumping back to the page's initial camera angle rather than the angle immediately before the strike.
After the scene has entered Rainy and is then switched to another season, the lightning button hides correctly, yet automatic blue lightning still appears after a random delay.
Clicking the lightning button in Rainy still highlights the button, plays thunder, and summons lightning, but the electric ring at the button edge no longer expands outward and quickly fades.

When the camera is dragged or zoomed in the Rainy scene, the white splash pattern slides relative to the pond shoreline like a screen-fixed noise layer instead of remaining attached to the water surface.
Most fireflies share the same movement direction and preserve their relative positions, making the group slide like a rigid cloud of light instead of drifting along individual flow paths.
Bushes and tree canopies still display correctly cut-out leaf silhouettes, but their shadows on the ground and near the tent appear as complete square or rectangular cards.

After an Edgeless note is selected and the canvas is continuously zoomed or panned, the note and its selection bounds move correctly, but the floating toolbar remains at the old screen position from the moment of selection and separates visibly from the note.

Short strokes draw and save normally, but once one continuously held long stroke reaches a certain length, the entire visible path suddenly collapses to its starting point, leaving only a dot. Further held movement adds nothing, and releasing still commits only that dot.

Pale-green regions revealed by mouse or touch trails expand but never contract afterward. Even after input stops and several seconds pass, traversed areas remain permanently exposed instead of being covered again by the dark-gray foreground.

If a movement key is already held before the doll turns to the red-light state and remains held, the character can keep moving during red light without failing. Pressing a movement key anew during red light still causes the normal failure.

When the vehicle accelerates, turns, or drifts on dry sandy terrain, its movement, wheels, and tracks remain normal, but no pale-brown dust is emitted behind the wheels. Water splashes remain unaffected.

After Séparer par secteur is enabled or disabled in the country-detail Bulles view, large and medium bubbles visibly pass through and overlap one another during the early rearrangement. Repulsion later recovers and the final sector lanes or aggregate layout still settles correctly.
The two paired point-light paths appear synchronized at first, but gradually drift out of phase over repeated loops, so the crossing highlight that should recur at a fixed interval keeps moving.

In the movie grid, pointing the mouse at a cover still highlights it and opens its details, but a cover targeted only by the center reticle receives no hover feedback and cannot be opened when the mouse is over blank space.

In Shaders / Integer Textures, after sand is continuously added above the wall and a small part of the wall is removed, blocked grains repeatedly favor the same diagonal direction. The pile drifts persistently left or right and forms stable directional bands instead of naturally splitting to both sides.

When scrolling from the opening chapter into the near-black learning chapter, the arch transition rises from the center and spreads outward instead of beginning at both sides and closing toward the center. Its final edge shape remains correct.

A short, fast sweep across an OUR PROJECTS card makes the local reveal suddenly balloon and tear across a large part of the card instead of remaining locally sized around the pointer. Slow pointer movement still produces a mostly normal image transition.

The first pinned canvas advances normally while scrolling down. After passing its midpoint and scrolling back up, it periodically flashes later, more complete building poses, creating brief reverse-direction jumps, then returns to the correct pose when scrolling stops.

Immediately downloading after changing the garment color, logo, or camera angle produces a PNG showing the appearance from roughly two seconds earlier even though the on-screen preview has updated. Waiting before downloading produces the current view.

When the mouse and center reticle target different movies at the same time, highlighting, scaling, click results, and detail content all follow the reticle target instead of the mouse target. Each input works correctly when used alone.

When black remains selected and the size changes from 14 inches to 16 inches, the color control still indicates black while the model itself becomes silver. Subsequent clicks on silver and black can still change the material normally.

While slowly scrolling from the Hero into Work, Ryde appears first, but YC Directory moves up and fades in while Library is still transparent, changing the order to Ryde, YC Directory, Library. Final content and layout are correct.

After either the 6.1-inch or 6.7-inch model is dragged to any non-front angle, switching sizes and returning resets that size to the default front view instead of restoring its previous viewing angle. The behavior affects both sizes.

After the hero workstation is dragged to a different viewing angle, the scene lighting moves with the viewpoint, causing the back of the monitor, the side of the computer, and the desk to become unnaturally bright from side or rear views. Lighting is normal immediately after a refresh before any drag.

Clicking Light or Dark in Settings correctly updates the theme, selected state, and saved preference message, but the page colors jump instantly to the final state instead of expanding from the upper right. The header theme button still performs the full expanding transition.

While the pointer moves within an OUR PROJECTS card, the local reveal area follows the pointer immediately, but its irregular fluid edge responds about 400 ms later. A slow entry first produces a smooth circular window before the organic edge appears, and on exit the area contracts before the edge disturbance fades.

When the pointer moves quickly and diagonally from one revealed OUR PROJECTS card into another, the departing card's local reveal position and area freeze for about 520 ms while the new card begins revealing immediately, leaving both cards active at once. Slow card-to-card movement or movement into blank space does not trigger it.
Each cleared cell still emits twelve light-colored particles, but exactly six are square and six are circular. Regular matches and cascades therefore mix sharp-cornered blocks with round bubbles.
In Physics / Vehicle, after the vehicle is driven or blocks are struck, an object remains clearly visible at a certain distance from the camera while its shadow abruptly disappears completely.

After a Pending order is accepted from the Recent Orders Pending list on the Dashboard, a success notification appears and the order detail shows Ready, but the current Pending list continues to show that order as Pending until the page is refreshed or revisited.
In Custom settings, increasing Grass Density step by step toward 100,000 continues to change the displayed value and rebuild the grass, but visible blade density stops increasing above 50,000.

When a Text Box is created and its side-middle handles are dragged to change width, the red bounds and handles use the full visible width, but text wraps roughly 80 pixels before the right edge. Short text is also shifted left within the bounds, leaving persistent extra blank space on the right.

When an object is dragged on a zoomed-in canvas, it moves increasingly ahead of the pointer as the drag continues, then abruptly jumps back near the release point when the mouse is released. The discrepancy does not appear at 100% zoom.

During continuous pointer movement, the outer ring remains perfectly concentric with the center and reaches every new position at the same time, eliminating the trailing and post-stop convergence of the outer ring. Hover colors and magnetic buttons still work.

During a day/night theme switch, the room walls and desk transition smoothly, but the plant on the right remains in the previous theme and then abruptly jumps to the new theme near the end of the room transition.

Hovering any corridor door still colors and partially pushes open the panel, but the handle remains completely stationary throughout the hover. Exit recovery and clicking to enter the room remain normal.

After any balloon in the SKILLS area of the ABOUT room is clicked, it bursts and shows the skill name normally, but never reappears after the text fades. Leaving ABOUT and returning still leaves that position empty.

During continuous panning in the Edgeless canvas, notes, cards, and selections move with the canvas while the dot grid stays fixed to the screen, making the content slide over it. Grid spacing still changes during zoom.

In one Edgeless stroke, after Shift is held to draw a horizontal segment, releasing Shift without releasing the pointer and then changing direction leaves the remainder locked to the same horizontal line. Free drawing returns only after that stroke ends.

The project information panel appears normally when the character enters the red carpet, but remains fixed at its initial screen position, size, and tilt while the character moves or the view turns, as if attached to the display. Leaving and re-entering updates its position once.

After the character genuinely leaves a triggered hex tile and later lands on or walks into it again, the tile returns to fully opaque orange and restarts its full disappearance delay, allowing its lifetime to be extended repeatedly. Jumping in place without landing again does not reset it.

During the middle of the transition from the Amsterdam street scene into Contact, the camera veers toward the left side of the screen and approaches the colorful building facade before returning to the correct endpoint. Start, end, and total duration remain unchanged.

In the BIRDS background of Experience, a fast sweep, slow movement, or prolonged presence in the same area all disperse the flock to approximately the same fixed extent instead of accumulating a stronger effect over time.

During an ordinary bobber splash, every droplet bends in the same tangential direction near its trajectory apex, briefly forming a shallow vortex instead of following its own radial parabola. Droplet count, start points, and landing points remain correct.

After the hero action button is clicked, the character faces the viewer and begins falling. The character's left arm, shown on the right side of the screen, briefly bends early in the fall and then straightens again; the rest of the fall remains normal.

When an object is dragged at a zoom other than 100%, its screen movement is incorrectly scaled: below 100% it continually lags behind the pointer, and above 100% it moves ahead. Releasing does not correct the offset, which becomes the final position.

After an Orbit drag is released from a viewpoint in front of the vehicle, the camera moves almost in step with the vehicle as it drives, keeping a front-facing view instead of naturally evolving toward the rear as the vehicle passes. The undragged path and rear-side releases remain normal.

When one continuous Highlighter stroke forms a loop, figure eight, or retraced path, genuinely overlapping portions within that same stroke become visibly darker while non-overlapping portions remain normal. A later separate stroke still blends normally where it crosses an earlier stroke.

For about the first 0.9 seconds after a day/night switch, the walls and desk intensify in the wrong direction beyond the old theme while the plant leaves overshoot the target theme and become over-tinted. Both then converge to the correct theme, and the final icon, text, and materials agree.

While slowly scrolling from the Hero into Work, the three project cards reveal in the correct order, but the room and monitor orientation lag the current scroll phase by several hundred milliseconds. Reversing immediately makes the yaw briefly continue in the old direction before settling after scrolling stops.

After the Growing Together counts and icon drawings complete, scrolling the section fully out of view and returning leaves the numbers at their final values, but the four icons erase in reverse and redraw in sequence, taking about 1.8 seconds to become complete again.

While the joystick remains held, a rapid reversal across its center immediately changes the character's facing and movement, but the inner handle stays in the old direction for about 330 ms before catching up to the new quadrant. It returns to center normally on release.

When a vertical globe drag crosses a pole, country fills continue rotating immediately with the pointer, but border outlines briefly retain the pre-crossing direction, sliding away from their countries before realigning about 420 ms later. The final orientation after release is correct.

On the first entrance into the “Subscribe. But why?” card, the dark-blue angled background still slides in from the right, but the email input group remains fixed at its final position throughout, so their relative positions keep changing during the entrance. The final layout is correct.

When a rectangle is dragged at a zoom other than 100%, the pointer and red selection bounds stay synchronized while the rectangle body preview remains one frame behind. On release, the body overshoots the correct endpoint and then rebounds into the selection bounds; the final position and history are correct.

In one Pen stroke, after Shift creates a horizontal segment, releasing Shift without releasing the pointer and continuing diagonally downward makes the visible tail curl backward into a brief hook before catching up to the pointer path about 320 ms later. The committed stroke is correct after release.

When a row- or column-clearing special is created from a four-piece match, its scale-in overlaps the final roughly 100 ms of the old center ingredient's fade. The same cell briefly shows the old ingredient, new special texture, and rotating highlight together; final type and position are correct.

After a door has colored and partially opened, briefly leaving and re-entering the same leaf within about 0.55 seconds keeps the panel colored and ajar, but the colored handle fades away by itself during the new hover. A full exit followed by re-entry restores it.

When no Gallery card is selected, quickly clicking two different cards makes the second card the current detail while the first remains flipped or expanded, leaving two cards open at once. The state resets only after leaving and re-entering the Gallery.

When the center moves from WERTE toward ZAHLEN while the outer ring is still in the WERTE phase, the outer ring becomes almost invisible against the light background for about 460 ms before recovering. The center remains correctly positioned and visible.

Pressing R while the vehicle is still visibly sliding, rotating, or bouncing returns it to the spawn position and orientation, but the pre-reset motion continues, making it slide, twist, or bounce at the spawn point.

If R is pressed to reset while the antenna is still swinging after a collision, the antenna first returns upright, then suddenly whips out again in the pre-reset swing direction before continuing to decay.

Immediately pressing Space or clicking again after one Cyber Lock ring succeeds causes the next ring to lock even though it is not aligned with the target line, advancing through the normal successful snap sequence.

During a fish fight, a short LINE fill shows only the left side of the color band, later colors appear progressively as tension rises, and disappear in reverse as it falls. Each fill width no longer contains the complete teal-to-gold-to-red gradient.

After the ball remains on the same block for a while and then leaves, the block counts the dwell time toward its post-contact delay and falls almost immediately instead of starting the normal delay when contact ends.

When the pointer moves quickly from one Features card to an adjacent card, the previous card's low-opacity background image remains for about 480 ms while the new card's image is already appearing. The old image disappears only afterward.
For roughly 900 ms after returning from a planet detail to the overview, every planet orbits at Earth's angular speed before recovering its own distinct speed.

After returning from any planet detail to the overview, planets resume one by one from the inner system outward at roughly 280 ms intervals, briefly leaving inner planets orbiting while outer planets remain frozen.

If Restart is clicked while an arrow is still in flight, the interface and values immediately return to the pre-start state, but the previous run's arrow continues flying on screen for about 1.1 seconds before disappearing.

After the player pauses and resumes at any point during a round, the timer resumes and the board remains interactive, but a later legal move that forms a three-piece match no longer starts resolution: the matched pieces remain in place, the score does not increase, and no falling, refill, or cascade follows. The same failure occurs when the game was paused while the board was idle.
